sources.cite: 17 U.S. Code Sec. 105 - Subject matter of copyright: United States Government works (Cornell LII)
sources.finding: Section 105 places all works of the United States Government (a work prepared by an officer or employee as part of official duties) in the public domain; such works are not eligible for copyright, hence cannot be released under a CC BY license.

sources.cite: Creative Commons, Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) legal code

opportunities.gap: The section repeatedly says to 'measure' contrast and 'you do not eyeball it, you check it' (lines 31, 51, 66) but never tells the learner HOW to obtain the ratio — no concrete tool, no input, no output description. This is the single load-bearing skill of the section and it is left implicit, weakening the Decision Rule's 'evidence check' (line 77) and Strong Reading Q1 (line 104), both of which reference 'the measured contrast ratio.'
opportunities.proposed_change: Add one concrete step in Worked Example step 1 (line 51) or the Core Concept Contrast bullet (line 31): open a contrast checker (e.g., the WebAIM Contrast Checker), paste the foreground hex (e.g., #BBBBBB) into Foreground Color and the background hex (#FFFFFF) into Background Color, and read the ratio; the tool instantly reports the number and a Pass/Fail against Normal Text (AA, 4.5:1) and Large Text (AA, 3:1). In PowerPoint, the built-in Accessibility Checker (Review > Check Accessibility) flags low-contrast and missing alt text as you author. This makes 'the measured contrast ratio' actionable.
